subject: Request: Time-sliced latency SLA addendum & burst reservation playbook
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@sierratech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sierratech.com>, procurement@sierratech.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification: Dedicated capacity guarantees (latency windows & burst)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough of the dedicated pool plan. Before we route the contract through procurement we need clarity on two items so our legal and SRE teams can sign off: 

1) Time-sliced latency guarantees: Our traffic has strong diurnal spikes and some short (10-20 minute) burst periods. We need an SLA addendum that commits to a 95th/99th latency target over rolling 10-minute windows during peak traffic, and a defined preemption behavior during those windows (soft preemption / best-effort vs. hard preemption).

2) Burst reservation playbook: We want an explicit on-paper process for temporary burst reservations (e.g., +20% capacity for up to 1 hour) including: how to request the burst, what notice is required, how billing is calculated, and fallback behavior if the burst cannot be served.

Attached is a traffic profile (sierra-traffic-profile.csv) and a redline of the draft SLA (redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf) with inline comments. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a time-sliced latency clause and an operational playbook for bursts? If not fully, what mitigations do you propose?

Appreciate a prompt response — procurement aims to finish the review by end of next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, SierraTech

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@sierratech.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification: Dedicated capacity guarantees (latency windows & burst)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for the attachments. Short answers up front: yes, we can put a time-sliced latency addendum on the table and we have an established burst reservation playbook; I want to loop in David for the implementation specifics and Ben for the commercial wording.

Next steps we propose:
- Technical addendum: Redwood will propose a 95th/99th latency objective measured over rolling 10-minute windows for pinned model variants. We will include explicit language about the "soft preemption" window (best-effort KV cache warming + graceful tail latency) vs. a small hard-preemption carveout for extreme multi-tenant events.
- Burst playbook draft: We'll provide a 3-step operational flow: request (API/console + email), instant reservation decision (if capacity available) or queued reservation with ETA, and billing (pro-rated hourly at the agreed burst rate).

David — can you prepare a short technical note describing queueing behavior, cache warming expectations, and the precise conditions where preemption would be applied? Ben and I will draft the legal phrasing and commercial impact. We aim to turn around a redline within 48 hours.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@sierratech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Clarification: Dedicated capacity guarantees (latency windows & burst)

Hi all — technical note below (pulling in engineering-runbook language so legal has concrete behavior). Quoting Samantha's ask for context: 

> "We need an SLA addendum that commits to a 95th/99th latency target over rolling 10-minute windows during peak traffic, and a defined preemption behavior during those windows (soft preemption / best-effort vs. hard preemption)."

1) Measurement and scope:
- Scope: pinned model variants running in SierraTech's dedicated pool. Measurements exclude client-side tokenization time and network RTT to customer VPC egress.
- Latency windows: we measure per-request tail latency at Redwood edge, aggregated into sliding 10-minute windows. Rolling window percentiles (95th/99th) are calculated every minute from the last 10 minutes to avoid boundary artifacts.

2) Soft vs. hard preemption behavior:
- Soft preemption (preferred): when the pool experiences short bursts that risk violating latency objectives, we first trigger adaptive batching and KV-cache prefetch prioritization for SierraTech's tenant routes. This preserves throughput while minimizing tail degradation. During soft preemption we will not evict in-flight tokens; instead we may temporarily prioritize SierraTech traffic if autoscaling headroom exists.
- Hard preemption (rare): applied only under severe capacity starvation (e.g., cluster-wide maintenance or critical hardware failure). Hard preemption may evict queued lower-priority requests after a configured grace period (default 30s). We will provide notice via webhook and Console alerting when hard preemption is active.

3) Burst reservation playbook (operational flow):
- Request: customer calls the console/API endpoint /reservations with desired delta and duration and marks urgency. We respond with an immediate accept/deny when spare capacity is available; otherwise we provide an ETA for reservation fulfillment.
- Fulfillment window: accepted bursts are reserved at the compute layer and pinned to SierraTech's tenant for the requested interval, with KV cache warmers triggered (best-effort) 2–5 minutes before the start when requested.
- Billing: pro-rated hourly at the agreed burst multiplier (default +20% capacity billed at 1.5x base rate). If a requested burst cannot be fulfilled, we offer crediting proportional to the unserved portion.

4) Observable signals and playbacks:
- We will expose a per-reservation trace (reservation_id) with expected activation time, actual start/end, and a post-event report showing 10-minute rolling latency percentiles during the reservation.

5) SLAs and remedies:
- Proposal: for rolling 10-minute windows during the agreed peak hours, Redwood will target 95th < 220ms and 99th < 450ms for standard pinned variants. Credits apply when measured 99th exceeds the threshold for >3 non-overlapping 10-minute windows in a 30-day period. Exact credit calculations to be handled by legal.

Open questions for contract language:
- Do you want the 10-minute window guarantee to apply 24/7 or only during contract-defined peak windows?
- Any hard cap on maximum hourly burst spend we should reflect?

I'll attach a concise runbook snippet for legal to pull text from.

—Dave
David Kim
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-runbook-snippet.txt

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@sierratech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@sierratech.com
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification: Dedicated capacity guarantees (latency windows & burst)

Hannah / David — this is exactly the level of detail we needed, thank you. A few quick confirmations from our side so procurement can proceed: 

- We will apply the rolling 10-minute percentile SLA only to the "peak hours" block (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT) — please reflect that in the addendum.
- The proposed 95th/99th targets (220ms / 450ms) look reasonable. We accept the credit trigger structure in principle; procurement will ask legal to propose the exact credit formula.
- For burst reservations: SierraTech would like an optional auto-warm flag for KV caches (we'll accept the 2–5 minute best-effort but want it opt-in).
- Maximum hourly burst spend: please cap at 3x our average hourly committed spend unless we opt-in to a higher cap.

If you can send the redline with those four items reflected, procurement will route it to legal and DocuSign. We appreciate the quick turnaround — aiming to sign next week.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Cloud Ops, SierraTech
